editorial.headline: A Protected Sea, Open to PMA Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This marine-park activity joins recreation with habitat preservation and sustainable ecosystems—and is open to full foreign ownership nationally, without Bali’s PMA moratorium blocking it.
editorial.body:
Marine park activity begins with a protected stretch of sea: a place that may be used for recreation, or reserved solely to conserve a particular habitat and sustain the ecosystem on which organisms there depend. The scope is deliberately broader than a single visitor experience or a single conservation purpose. It describes a protected marine area whose public and ecological roles may coexist, or whose preservation role may stand on its own. The reference points named in the record—Pahawang Marine Park in Lampung, Raja Ampat Marine Park in West Papua, and Gili Matra Marine Park in NTB—make the setting concrete without narrowing the activity to any one of them.

Nationally, the activity is open to PMA registration. Foreign ownership may reach 100%, under the source cited as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is a clear national ownership position: there is no lower foreign-ownership ceiling in the record for this activity. Nor does the record’s list of open business scales identify a particular scale. That absence should be kept intact; the record establishes a national PMA opening, but does not supply a scale-based distinction for registration.

Bali changes neither the national ceiling nor the nature of the activity. The province’s permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK in Bali and described as medium-high/high risk, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest local conclusion is straightforward: a foreigner can register this activity in Bali today, not merely elsewhere in Indonesia. The record nevertheless calls for verification at the address in question.

The resulting picture is precise. A marine park is not defined only by leisure or only by preservation; it can serve a protected area’s recreational use, habitat conservation, and sustainable ecosystem aim. Full foreign ownership is available nationally. In Bali, the stated moratorium does not close the activity because its recorded risk placement sits outside the two blocked bands. Address-level verification remains the local point carried by the record.
